summary: Adds branded Google, Microsoft, and Apple cloud-signup choices, isolated multi-secret API configuration delivery, and verified Microsoft Entra multi-organization OIDC support.
userImpact: Cloud signup presents the existing branded Google, Microsoft, and Apple controls when those independently configured providers are available, without sharing provider credentials.
Microsoft work or school accounts can use a multi-organization Entra registration while personal Microsoft accounts remain excluded.

instructions: Use apiConfigBundle.secrets only with a signed host chart that advertises the v2 contract; the legacy single-secret form remains supported.

configuration: apiConfigBundle.secrets accepts up to 16 unique EG_CONFIG_BUNDLE_* environment bindings backed by dedicated non-optional Secret keys in the API container only.

changes: The generic OIDC runtime recognizes the exact Microsoft Entra organizations issuer and validates each signed token against its UUID tenant claim and reconstructed tenant-specific issuer.

security: Each provider credential remains in a dedicated Kubernetes Secret key and is projected only as its declared EG_CONFIG_BUNDLE_* environment variable in the split API container.
The chart rejects shared runtime Secret aliases, duplicate environment names, arbitrary environment namespaces, mixed legacy/v2 forms, and credential inheritance by workers or jobs.
Entra organizations tokens require a UUID tid whose reconstructed tenant issuer exactly matches the signed iss claim before JWT verification succeeds.
knownLimitations: External Google, Microsoft, and Apple application registrations and live consent journeys remain deployment acceptance steps.
rollback: Redeploy the previous host chart and shared package, then use the legacy single-secret bundle form; no database rollback is required.
validation: Focused Helm tests cover v1 compatibility, v2 multi-secret rendering, schema rejection, and API-only isolation.
Focused OIDC tests cover Entra organizations discovery, tenant-specific signed-token acceptance, and issuer/tid mismatch rejection.
The signup page regression test covers all three branded provider controls and preserves the fail-closed no-provider state.
